source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the Ernst Mayr biographical profile printed on PDF page 2; unit front matter, not Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to the profile, when was Ernst Mayr born?
questions.explanation: The profile gives his birth date as 5 July 1904.
questions.source_text: Born on 5 July 1904, in Kempten, Germany

questions.question: Ernst Mayr was born in:
questions.explanation: The profile identifies Kempten, Germany as his birthplace.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr is described in the profile as a Harvard University:
questions.explanation: The profile calls Mayr a Harvard University evolutionary biologist.

questions.question: Which title was used for Ernst Mayr in the profile?
questions.explanation: The profile says Mayr has been called ‘The Darwin of the 20th century’.
questions.source_text: who has been called ‘The Darwin of the 20th century’

questions.question: In which year did Ernst Mayr join Harvard’s Faculty of Arts and Sciences?
questions.explanation: The profile states that Mayr joined the faculty in 1953.
questions.source_text: Mayr joined Harvard’s Faculty of Arts and Sciences in 1953

questions.question: In which year did Ernst Mayr retire from Harvard’s Faculty of Arts and Sciences?
questions.explanation: The profile gives 1975 as the year he retired.

questions.question: After retirement, Mayr assumed the title:
options: Alexander Agassiz Professor of Zoology Emeritus
questions.explanation: The profile names his post-retirement title as Alexander Agassiz Professor of Zoology Emeritus.
questions.source_text: assuming the title Alexander Agassiz Professor of Zoology Emeritus

questions.question: Which fields are explicitly listed as areas of Mayr’s research?
questions.explanation: The profile lists ornithology, taxonomy, zoogeography, evolution, systematics, and the history and philosophy of biology. Astrophysics is not listed.
questions.source_text: his research spanned ornithology, taxonomy, zoogeography, evolution, systematics, and the history and philosophy of biology

questions.question: According to the profile, Mayr helped make which question central to evolutionary biology?
options: The origin of the solar system
questions.explanation: The profile says he made the origin of species diversity a central question of evolutionary biology.
questions.source_text: made the origin of species diversity the central question of evolutionary biology

questions.question: The profile credits Ernst Mayr with pioneering the currently accepted definition of a:
questions.explanation: The profile explicitly says he pioneered the currently accepted definition of a biological species.
questions.source_text: He also pioneered the currently accepted definition of a biological species.

questions.question: Match the award with the year in which Ernst Mayr received it, as listed in the profile.
questions.explanation: The profile lists the Balzan Prize in 1983, the International Prize for Biology in 1994, and the Crafoord Prize in 1999.
questions.source_text: the Balzan Prize in 1983, the International Prize for Biology in 1994, and the Crafoord Prize in 1999

questions.question: According to the profile, Ernst Mayr died in:
questions.explanation: The profile says Mayr died at the age of 100 in 2004.
questions.source_text: Mayr died at the age of 100 in the year 2004.
